Computing Consumer Tech Space & Aerospace Earnings Menu Money & Markets Economic Indicators Markets Personal Finance Earnings Menu Lifestyle Cars & Bikes Collecting Entertainment Food & Fine Dining Health and Fitness Real Estate Travel General Trivia Election Day is not a federal holiday: What's open and closed on Nov. 3, 2026 
 Election Day is not a federal holiday in 2026, so banks, post offices, supermarkets and stock markets stay open on Nov. 3 while some schools close
 1 / 12 List slides Election Day is not a federal holiday: What's open and closed on Nov. 3, 2026 List slides Previous Start over By Colleen Cabili · Updated November 3, 2026 Add QZ to Google Illustration: Quartz
 The vote that decides which party controls Congress takes place on an ordinary Tuesday. On Nov. 3, 2026, most Americans will work, run errands and pay bills on the same day the polls are open. That overlap raises a practical question every two years: Is Election Day a holiday, and what will be closed?
 The short answer is no. Election Day does not appear on the list of federal holidays set in law. Federal offices keep their normal schedules. So do the Federal Reserve and most banks. Federal law fixes the date as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. In 2026, that puts the general election on Nov. 3.
 The 2026 contest is a midterm. All 435 seats in the U.S. House are on the ballot. About a third of the Senate is up as well, along with many state and local offices.
 The routines of daily life largely continue on a day that is not a federal holiday. Mail is delivered. The New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq $NDAQ open for trading. Supermarkets, pharmacies and large retailers are generally open, though hours vary by store and location.
 The picture is less uniform at the state and local level. Some states treat Election Day as a holiday or give state employees the day off. Many states require employers to give workers time to vote. Those rules differ on whether the time is paid, how much is allowed and how much notice is needed. Some school districts close because their buildings serve as polling places. Others turn the day into a teacher training or remote-learning day. Polling hours also differ from state to state.
 Proposals to make Election Day a federal holiday have been introduced in Congress, including as part of the Freedom to Vote Act. None has become law.
 The 10 sections below take the main questions in turn. They start with the day's federal status and the 2026 date. Next come banks, the Postal Service, stock markets, grocery stores and pharmacies, and major retailers. The last three cover schools, government offices and time off to vote. Local arrangements are set by states, school districts, employers and individual stores. Readers should confirm the details that apply where they live and work.
 Is Election Day a federal holiday 
 Illustration: Quartz
 No. Election Day is not one of the federal holidays set in law. It is a regular workday for the federal government and for most private employers.
 The list of federal holidays sits in Title 5 of the U.S. Code, in section 6103. It names 11 permanent holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Washington's Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. Election Day is not among them.
 Federal workers get a weekday off when a holiday lands on a weekend. A Saturday holiday is generally observed on the Friday before. A Sunday holiday is generally observed on the Monday after. Election Day would never need that rule. It always falls on a Tuesday.
 The November calendar puts the gap in plain view. Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, eight days after the vote. Federal offices close for it. The election itself takes place on a working Tuesday.
 A federal holiday has a narrower reach than many people assume. The designation governs the federal workforce and the operations of federal agencies. It does not require private companies to close. It also does not require them to give employees a paid day off. Businesses set their own holiday schedules, and many follow the federal calendar only in part.
 That limit shapes the debate over the vote. Making Election Day a federal holiday would close federal offices and give federal employees the day off. On its own, it would not guarantee time off for someone who works at a store, a restaurant or a hospital.
 Members of Congress have introduced bills over the years to make Election Day a federal holiday. The Freedom to Vote Act, a broad voting-rights package, included that change. It did not clear the Senate. None of the proposals has become law.
 Congress can add to the list when it chooses to. Juneteenth, observed on June 19, is the newest entry. It was created by the Juneteenth National Independence Day Act, which President Joe Biden signed. The addition before that was Martin Luther King Jr. Day, which President Ronald Reagan signed into law in 1983.
 States are a separate matter. A state can close its own offices on Election Day even though the federal government does not. The rules where a person lives can differ from the national picture.
 Election Day 2026 date: Tuesday, Nov. 3 
 Illustration: Quartz
 The 2026 general election falls on Tuesday, Nov. 3. Federal law sets Election Day as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, and the first Monday of November 2026 is Nov. 2.
 The exact wording of that rule matters. It does not call for the first Tuesday of the month. It calls for the Tuesday that follows the first Monday. Under that formula, Election Day can never land on Nov. 1. The earliest possible date is Nov. 2, and the latest is Nov. 8.
 The 2026 vote is a midterm election. Midterms take place halfway through a presidential term, so no presidential race appears on the ballot. Every seat in the U.S. House of Representatives is up for election. House members serve two-year terms, which is why the full chamber is contested in every even-numbered year.
 Senate races are on the ballot as well. Senators serve six-year terms on a staggered schedule, so only part of the chamber faces voters in any one cycle. The combined House and Senate results decide which party controls Congress for the next two years.
 Federal contests share the ballot with state and local races. Depending on where a voter lives, those can include governors, state legislators, judges, county officials, school board members and ballot measures. A sample ballot from the local election office shows which races apply to a given address.
 The date is uniform across the country, but polling hours are not. Each state sets its own hours, and no single opening or closing time applies nationwide. A polling place in one state can still be open after polls in another state have closed. State and local election offices post the hours and polling locations for each precinct.
 Voters who are already in line when polls close are generally allowed to cast a ballot. The rules on this point differ by state. Anyone cutting it close should check their local election office's guidance before leaving home.
 Staggered closing times across several time zones also shape election night. Results come in over the course of the evening. Close races can take longer to call while election officials finish counting ballots.
 Are banks open on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Banks are open on Election Day, and the Federal Reserve keeps its regular schedule. For the banking system, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, is an ordinary business day.
 The reason comes down to the Federal Reserve's calendar. Most U.S. banks close on the days the Fed is closed. Those days track the federal holiday list, which includes Thanksgiving and Christmas but not Election Day. When the Fed is open, the payment systems that move money between banks are running too. Most lenders keep their branches open as a result.
 That matters for anyone expecting money to move on Election Day. Direct deposits, bill payments and transfers scheduled for Nov. 3 should process on a normal business-day timeline. No holiday delay pushes them to the next day, as would happen on a Fed holiday.
 Credit unions generally follow the same pattern. Many align their closures with the Fed's schedule for the same reason commercial banks do. They rely on the same payment networks to settle transactions.
 Branch hours are still set by each bank and can differ from one location to another. A branch that keeps shorter hours in a smaller town, or closes early on certain days, will keep its usual hours on Election Day. The bank's website or app lists the hours for each branch.
 Customers who plan to vote before or after work and want to skip a branch visit have other options. ATMs, mobile apps and online banking work around the clock, holiday or not. Mobile check deposits and transfers between accounts do not require a branch at all.
 The calendar changes eight days later. Veterans Day is a federal holiday, and the Fed is closed for it. In 2026 it falls on Wednesday, Nov. 11. Some banks close that day while others stay open. Transactions scheduled for it typically move to the next business day. Anyone timing a payment around early November should keep the two dates separate.
 Does the U.S. Postal Service deliver mail on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Yes. The U.S. Postal Service delivers mail on Election Day, and post offices keep their regular hours on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Letter carriers run their usual routes. Retail counters stay open for stamps, packages and other services.
 The reason is the federal calendar. The Postal Service closes on federal holidays, and Election Day is not one of them. Residential delivery, business delivery and P.O. box access all follow their normal schedule.
 An open post office matters most to voters who cast ballots by mail. Every state lets at least some voters use an absentee ballot. Many states send a mail ballot to any registered voter who requests one, with no excuse required.
 Mail delivery on Election Day does not guarantee that a ballot mailed that morning will count. Each state sets its own deadline for returned ballots. Some require a ballot to reach election officials by the time polls close. Others accept ballots that arrive later, as long as they carry a postmark dated on or before Election Day. Voters should check their own state's rule well ahead of Nov. 3.
 The postmark itself depends on timing. A letter dropped in a blue collection box after the day's last pickup may not be postmarked until the next day. Each collection box lists its pickup times. A voter who brings a ballot to a post office retail counter can ask a clerk to apply a postmark by hand.
 Many states also let voters skip the mail entirely. Depending on the state, a completed ballot can go directly to a local election office or into an official ballot drop box. Election officials run those options, not the Postal Service.
 Private carriers keep normal schedules as well. UPS and FedEx $FDX do not list Election Day among the holidays when they suspend service.
 Bill payments, online orders and certified letters move through the system on their usual timetable. Anything with a deadline on Nov. 3 needs the same mailing lead time as it would on any other weekday.
 Is the stock market open on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 The New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq $NDAQ are open on Election Day. On Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, both exchanges will run a full regular session from 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern time.
 Stock exchanges set their own holiday calendars rather than copying the federal list. The NYSE closes for 10 holidays a year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Nasdaq follows the same schedule. Election Day does not appear on either calendar.
 The market and federal calendars differ in both directions. Good Friday is not a federal holiday, but the exchanges close for it. Columbus Day and Veterans Day are federal holidays, but stocks trade normally on both.
 The bond market runs on a separate calendar. U.S. bond trading follows holiday recommendations from the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association, known as SIFMA. The group recommends a full bond-market close on Veterans Day, Nov. 11, even though stock exchanges stay open that day. Election Day is not a bond-market holiday, and bonds trade on their usual schedule.
 Most election results arrive after the closing bell. The earliest polls in the country close at 6 p.m. Eastern time. That is two hours after regular stock trading ends. Nearly all vote counts are therefore reported once the regular session is over.
 Some trading continues into the evening. Many brokers offer after-hours sessions for individual stocks. Stock index futures on CME $CME Group's platform trade nearly around the clock during the week. The first full regular stock session after polls close is Wednesday, Nov. 4.
 For ordinary investors, Election Day works like any other trading day. Orders placed during market hours execute as usual. U.S. stock trades have settled one business day after the trade since May 2024. A purchase made on Election Day therefore settles on Wednesday.
 The next full market closure after the election is Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. On the following day, Friday, Nov. 27, the stock market closes early at 1 p.m. Eastern time.
 Are grocery stores and pharmacies open on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Grocery stores and pharmacies are generally open on Election Day. In 2026 that day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Supermarkets and drugstores across the U.S. typically keep their regular weekday schedules.
 No federal law requires private businesses to close for Election Day. Supermarket chains and pharmacy companies set their own operating calendars. Those calendars usually reserve closures for a handful of major holidays, such as Christmas Day. Election Day does not typically appear on those closure calendars.
 Hours are the part that varies. A supermarket in a dense city may keep different hours from one in a small town, even under the same brand. Franchised and independently owned grocers can set their own schedules. The only reliable way to confirm a specific store's hours is to check that location directly, through the company's website, its app or a phone call.
 Pharmacies add a second layer. The pharmacy counter inside a supermarket or drugstore often keeps shorter hours than the store around it. A store can be open while its pharmacy is closed. Anyone picking up a prescription should check the pharmacy hours specifically, not just the store's. Some drugstore chains operate 24-hour locations, but those are a minority of stores and are not found in every area.
 Refill tools can cut down on waiting at the counter. Large pharmacy chains such as CVS and Walgreens $WBA let customers request refills online or through an app and get a notice when an order is ready.
 State rules do not change the picture much. In states that give government employees Election Day off, that designation applies to public offices, not to private grocery or drug stores. Shoppers in those states can expect the same general pattern as everywhere else: stores open, with hours set location by location.
 Look up the specific store and its pharmacy counter before heading out on Nov. 3. Both can post hours that differ from a neighboring location.
 Walmart, Target, Costco and Kroger on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Walmart $WMT , Target $TGT , Costco $COST and Kroger stores are generally open on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. None of the four chains treats the day as a store holiday. Shoppers can expect an ordinary Tuesday, with hours set by each location.
 The holidays these chains close for make up a short list, and Election Day is not on it. Walmart and Target close their U.S. stores on Christmas Day. Both have also closed on Thanksgiving in recent years. Costco keeps a longer closure calendar than most big-box retailers. Its U.S. warehouses close on New Year's Day, Easter Sunday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. Election Day falls outside that pattern.
 Kroger is a family of grocery brands as well as a single store name. The Cincinnati-based company runs supermarkets under banners that include Ralphs, Fred Meyer, King Soopers, Harris Teeter, Fry's, Smith's and Dillons. A shopper in Denver or Los Angeles may never see the Kroger name on a storefront. The neighborhood King Soopers or Ralphs still belongs to the same company and is generally open on Election Day too.
 Walmart also owns Sam's Club, the membership warehouse chain that competes most directly with Costco . At both warehouse chains, membership is the main practical hurdle. Shopping there generally requires a card, whatever the day.
 Hours inside a single store can differ by department. Pharmacy counters, vision centers, tire and auto service bays and fuel stations at Walmart and Costco often keep shorter schedules than the main sales floor. Some voters plan to pick up a prescription or fill a gas tank on the way to or from the polls. They should check the hours for that department, not just the building.
 Each of the four companies posts location-level hours through its website and app store locator. Those pages show the schedule for a specific store. Severe weather, staffing or a store-specific event can still change hours on any given day. Election Day does not change them on its own.
 Why some schools close on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Some public schools close on Election Day because their buildings double as polling places. The choice belongs to each school district. One district may cancel classes on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, while a neighboring district holds a regular school day.
 Schools are a common choice for polling sites. They are public buildings spread across most communities. Many have large open rooms, such as gymnasiums and cafeterias, that can hold voting booths, check-in tables and lines of voters. Many also have parking lots and accessible entrances.
 That convenience creates a scheduling problem for districts. On a normal school day, the building is full of students and staff. On Election Day, it is also open to members of the public. Voters come in from the time polls open until they close. Some districts respond by giving students the day off. That way, the building does not have to run classes and an election at the same time.
 Not every district that hosts voters cancels school outright. Some turn the date into a teacher in-service day. Students stay home, and teachers report for training or planning. Other districts switch to remote learning. Instruction continues online while the building serves voters.
 No national rule tells schools whether to open or close on Election Day. Districts typically settle the question when their school board approves the academic calendar for the year. Private and parochial schools follow their own calendars. They may make a different decision from the local public district.
 Schools are only one type of polling location. Election officials also use libraries, community centers, churches and other public spaces, depending on the area. A district whose buildings are not used for voting has less reason to change its schedule.
 Parents planning for Nov. 3 can find the answer on their district's published academic calendar or website. Checking early leaves time to arrange child care if classes are canceled. Families with children in more than one school system should check each calendar separately.
 Are government offices, DMVs and courts open on Election Day 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Federal government offices are open on Election Day, which is absent from the federal holiday calendar. State and local offices, including DMVs and courthouses, generally keep their regular hours unless a state or local government has chosen to close them.
 Federal agencies run on a normal schedule that day. Social Security Administration field offices follow the federal holiday calendar. So do Internal Revenue Service offices and passport agencies. That calendar does not include Election Day.
 The nearest federal holiday after the 2026 vote is Veterans Day. It falls on Wednesday, Nov. 11, eight days after Election Day. Anyone planning a visit to a federal office around the election should expect closures on that date, not on Nov. 3.
 The federal court system works the same way. U.S. district courts, bankruptcy courts and federal appeals courts observe federal holidays only. Cases scheduled for Election Day proceed unless a judge or clerk says otherwise.
 State government is a separate question. A state that makes Election Day a legal holiday may close its own offices. That choice can also reach state courts and agencies. The list of states that do this has changed over time. The reliable check is the state's official website or its court system calendar.
 Motor vehicle offices are run by states, and in some places by counties or cities. Closure decisions rest with those agencies. Many DMVs let residents renew a license or vehicle registration online. Those services do not depend on office hours.
 County clerks and municipal courts set their own schedules. Some public buildings, such as town halls, community centers and libraries, double as polling places. That can affect parking, entrances and room access for other business on the day.
 Local election offices carry a heavier load than usual. County and city election staff run polling sites, answer voter questions and count ballots after polls close.
 Anyone with an appointment, court hearing or jury summons on Nov. 3 should confirm it with the office that issued it. Assuming a closure can lead to a missed date.
 Time off to vote and states with an Election Day holiday 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Most American workers get no automatic day off for Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Many states, however, require employers to give employees time to vote. Some states go further and treat Election Day as a state holiday or a day off for state employees.
 Voting-leave laws are written state by state, and they differ in three main ways. Some states require the time off to be paid, while others allow it to be unpaid. States also set different limits on how many hours a worker can take. Many attach conditions, such as how much advance notice an employee must give before taking the time.
 Some state laws also tie the leave to a worker's schedule. In those states, an employer may not have to grant time off if the polls are open for a set window before or after the employee's shift. The details depend on the state. A worker in one state cannot assume the protections that apply in another.
 A state holiday works differently from a voting-leave law. When a state designates Election Day as a holiday, the designation typically covers state government employees. It generally does not require private businesses to close or give staff the day off. Private employers can still choose to do so. Some companies offer paid time to vote as a matter of company policy.
 Lists of states with an Election Day holiday change as legislatures pass new laws. Current information from your own state is the most reliable guide. The secretary of state or state election office posts voting rules, and the state labor department typically publishes guidance on voting leave for workers.
 Early voting and mail ballots offer another route for people who cannot get away from work on Nov. 3. Many states let voters cast a ballot in person during an early-voting period before Election Day. Many also allow voters to return a ballot by mail. Eligibility rules and deadlines differ by state. Some states require voters to give a reason before they can vote by mail. Checking those rules well before November gives workers options that do not depend on getting time off.
